inputs.prompt: One original Maskglass Corsair, a human female swordswoman facing RIGHT in locked three-quarter orthographic game view. Silver mirror half-mask over the screen-left side of the face, visible other eye and mouth, long brown tied-back hair, ragged muted grey-green scarf and skirt strips, ivory sleeves, charcoal trousers, brown leather boots and belt with a small brass bottle. Exactly TWO arms, TWO hands and TWO legs. RIGHT hand at screen-left grips the gold basket hilt of ONE complete curved SILVER SABER, blade initially raised above her shoulder as in the first reference. LEFT arm at screen-right holds ONE round dark buckler with a brass rim, central boss and radial brass spokes. Keep the saber blade rigid, full length and continuously attached to its hilt; keep the buckler round and on the same arm. Preserve face, mask, clothing, both grips and body proportions. Locked camera, fixed body scale and ground baseline; full figure, blade tip and shield remain visible. Every background pixel stays flat saturated BLUE, constant neutral illumination. Slow controlled physical cut from the supplied raised-saber windup to the supplied rightward extended contact pose. Right shoulder rotates forward, elbow extends and wrist guides the SAME rigid gently curved metal blade down toward the RIGHT. Keep the blade narrow and its tip connected to the full-length steel blade at every instant. Sharp painted metal outline in every frame, no motion blur, no crescent trail, no slash effect, no blade stretching or detached pieces. Left arm retains its buckler. Stop at the contact pose and hold it; no recovery or second swing.
